title: Touch Control Error
shortDescription: A touch control button is stuck or shorted.
fullDescription:
F2 on a Whirlpool induction or radiant cooktop indicates the control detected a touch input held continuously. Spilled liquid or a cracked touch panel is the usual cause.

Wipe the surface dry and allow the cooktop to rest. If F2 persists, the touch board likely needs replacement.

fixSteps.title: Clean surface
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe with a dry microfiber cloth; remove any wet items from the touch area.

fixSteps.title: Power reset
fixSteps.instruction: Flip the breaker off for 5 minutes, then on.

fixSteps.title: Replace touch board
fixSteps.instruction: If code persists, replace the user interface board.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the glass is cracked — glass replacement is a specialty job.
videoSearchQuery: Whirlpool cooktop F2 touch error fix

faq.a: Moisture wicked under the glass edge can keep a capacitive touch triggered.

title: Cooktop Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: A surface temperature sensor reported out-of-range values.
fullDescription:
F3 is shown when one of the under-glass thermistors reports readings the control cannot trust. A damaged sensor or pinched lead wire is typical.

Identify which burner triggers F3 and inspect its sensor and harness.

fixSteps.title: Remove glass
fixSteps.instruction: Access the cooktop underside per service manual to reach the thermistor.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new thermistor and route harness clear of heating elements.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro — disassembling a glass cooktop without damage takes practice.

faq.q: Can I use other burners with F3?
faq.a: Sometimes yes — the control may lock out only the affected element.

title: Overtemp Shutdown
shortDescription: The cooktop shut a burner down for overheating.
fullDescription:
F4 is triggered when a burner's temperature sensor exceeds the maximum allowed value. This typically happens when an empty pan is left on a high setting, or when a cookware base does not contact the glass evenly.

Allow the element to cool fully. Use flat-bottomed induction-compatible cookware on induction models.

fixSteps.title: Cool down
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cookware and allow the element to cool for 15-30 minutes.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro only if F4 occurs with proper cookware and the correct power level.

faq.q: Is the glass damaged after F4?
faq.a: Usually no — the shutoff is designed to protect the glass.

title: Cooling Fan Fault
shortDescription: The internal cooling fan is not operating correctly.
fullDescription:
F5 indicates the cooling fan beneath the cooktop did not reach expected RPM. The fan keeps induction power electronics within safe temperature.

Blocked airflow under the cabinet, debris in the fan, or a failed motor can trigger it.

fixSteps.title: Clear vents
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure the cabinet installation has required clearances per manual.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: Access underside and install a new cooling fan assembly.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if you need to remove the cooktop to service the fan.

faq.q: Can I run the cooktop with F5?
faq.a: No — the induction driver will overheat within minutes.

title: Line Voltage Out of Range
shortDescription: Incoming voltage is too high or too low.
fullDescription:
F6 is reported when input voltage falls outside the expected 200-250 V range. Incorrect wiring at installation, brownouts, or a loose lug can all cause this.

Confirm the breaker and terminal block voltage with a meter before suspecting the cooktop.

fixSteps.title: Check breaker
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the double-pole breaker is fully on and not tripped.

fixSteps.title: Call electrician
fixSteps.instruction: If voltage at the terminal is out of spec, hire an electrician.

whenToCallPro: Always involve a licensed electrician for 240 V diagnostics.

faq.a: Usually not — it typically reflects a household wiring or utility problem.

title: Induction Generator Fault
shortDescription: An induction power module reported an internal fault.
fullDescription:
F7 points to a problem inside an induction generator (power module). Only induction cooktops produce this code. Modules can fail from heat stress or component aging.

Replacement requires removing the cooktop and is considered a professional repair.

fixSteps.title: Identify module
fixSteps.instruction: Note which burner triggers F7 — one generator typically drives two zones.

whenToCallPro: Always — induction modules require proper grounding and torque.

faq.q: Can I still use unaffected burners?
faq.a: Often yes — the other generator remains functional.

title: Relay Fault
shortDescription: A control relay is stuck or failed.
fullDescription:
F8 indicates the control senses a relay contact that did not change state as commanded. Relays live on the main control board and can weld shut from inrush current.

This is a control board replacement in most cases.
symptoms: Burner heats with no command or won't heat at all

fixSteps.title: Disconnect power
fixSteps.instruction: Turn the breaker off immediately — a stuck relay is a safety hazard.

fixSteps.title: Replace control board
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new main control board.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro — stuck relays can energize burners unexpectedly.

faq.a: Treat it as one. Cut power at the breaker until repaired.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: UI and main control have lost communication.
fullDescription:
F9 shows when the user interface and main control board cannot exchange data. A damaged ribbon cable or failed board is typical.

Power cycle first. If code returns, replace the suspect board after harness inspection.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Flip breaker off 10 minutes, back on.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cables
fixSteps.instruction: Open underside and reseat inter-board ribbons.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if reseating does not resolve F9.

faq.a: The control disables burners as a precaution.

title: Generic Control Error
shortDescription: A non-specific control error was detected.
fullDescription:
Er is a catch-all fault shown on some Whirlpool cooktops when the control cannot classify the error. A power reset clears most transient Er events.

If Er returns immediately, note whether any burner is in use and consult the service manual for the extended sub-code.

fixSteps.title: Power reset
fixSteps.instruction: Flip breaker off 5 minutes and back on.

fixSteps.title: Enter diagnostics
fixSteps.instruction: Refer to service manual to pull the underlying sub-code.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if Er returns within minutes of reset.

faq.a: Not always — but it warrants diagnosis if it keeps returning.

title: Child Lock Active
shortDescription: The control lock has been engaged.
fullDescription:
C (or a lock icon alongside) means child lock is on. This is a normal state, not a fault. Burners are disabled until the lock is cleared.

Hold the lock button for 3 seconds to disable.

fixSteps.title: Unlock
fixSteps.instruction: Press and hold the lock button for 3 seconds.

faq.q: Does C turn on by itself?
faq.a: No — it requires a deliberate long-press to engage.

title: Control fault
fullDescription: Cooktop control board fault. Standard troubleshooting on Whirlpool cooktop usually involves resetting power and checking the implicated component.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power for 5 minutes, then restore.

fixSteps.title: Inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Visual inspection of the implicated component.

fixSteps.title: Test/replace
fixSteps.instruction: Test sensor with multimeter or replace if reading abnormal.

whenToCallPro: If sensor replacement doesn't resolve, control board may need replacement.

faq.q: Can I still use the oven?
faq.a: Resolve before extended use to prevent further damage.
